sources.confirmed_definition: Shapiro defines the duct friction coefficient f as the ratio of wall shearing stress to the dynamic head of the stream, i.e. f = tau_w / (0.5 rho u^2), and uses the differential friction parameter 4 f dx / D.

evidence_boundary: The factor-of-four conversion is no longer inferred from the letter Cf alone. It follows from Jin explicitly sourcing the equations to Shapiro [51], Shapiro's wall-shear/dynamic-head definition, the common 4 f dx/D form, and the repository's explicit Darcy-friction source definition.
This record resolves only the coefficient convention. It does not provide the numerical Cf value used by Jin for Fig. 14.
Liu et al.'s separate negligible-wall-friction analysis is not used to set Jin's Cf to zero.
If an author-provided Fig. 14 dataset later defines Cf differently for that calculation, the higher-specificity source must override this mapping and the evidence record must be revised.
